messages:
amanda.release: Heads up — promo to prod is blocked, deploy-bot flagged an image manifest digest mismatch when promoting canary 2026-03 build. Can we triage quickly? :eyes:

deploy-bot: Promotion halted for tag redwood/api-service:2026-03-canary because manifest digest comparison failed between staging registry (gcr.io/redwood-staging) and prod registry (gcr.io/redwood-prod). Root image digest differs: staging sha256:aa11... vs prod sha256:bb22...

chris.sre: I'm looking. Early suspicion: same layers but different compression metadata changed the layer digests when re-uploading to prod mirror.

ben.infra: Confirming — ran regctl and skopeo inspect, layer sizes identical but digests differ. Output: ```
$ skopeo inspect docker://gcr.io/redwood-staging/api-service:2026-03-canary --raw | jq '.layers[] | {size: .size, digest: .digest}'
{"size": 1248123, "digest": "sha256:111aaa..."}
{"size": 4096, "digest": "sha256:222bbb..."}
```
vs prod: ```
{"size": 1248123, "digest": "sha256:333ccc..."}
{"size": 4096, "digest": "sha256:444ddd..."}
```
Compression bits look different.

amanda.release: So same content but different digests — that would block immutability checks in our deploy flow. What's the roll/hold plan?

chris.sre: Short term — pin the promo to last-good image sha256:zz99good... and keep canary traffic on current prod image. I'll add a manual hold to the release.

ben.infra: Long term we should make the image republish deterministic. Likely culprit: gzip timestamps or different tar / gzip flags used in the build agents in eu-west vs us-central mirror pushers. Our registry mirrors recompress on upload if streaming, producing different compressed bytes and therefore different layer digests.

sara.oncall: I can run a one-off re-push from the builder artifact store (we have the exact tar blobs) to prod with --no-change compression flags and a reproducible gzip ( --no-name / --no-time ) so digests match. Need approval to do that.

amanda.release: Approve — do the re-push and report back. We'll keep the promo pinned and update release notes with a note that canary was held due to manifest digest inconsistency.

chris.sre: Action plan: 1) pin promotion to sha256:zz99good... (done) 2) sara: re-push artifact from builder with deterministic gzip flags to prod mirror (sara to run) 3) regbot verify manifests and re-run deploybot promotion, 4) if digests match, unhold and promote; else rollback to manual release and open infra ticket.

sara.oncall: Starting re-push now. Command I'm using: ```
regctl image copy --no-compress --source gcs://builds/api-service/2026-03-canary.tar 
  docker://gcr.io/redwood-prod/api-service:2026-03-canary --gzip-opts=--no-name --gzip-opts=--no-time
```
I'll post logs in a sec.

ben.infra: FYI adding a ticket to infra: "docker push non-deterministic compression -> manifest digest drift across mirrors" with proposed fix: standardize builder gzip flags and prefer pushing canonical blobs to registry (avoid on-the-fly re-compression).

(2m later) sara.oncall: Re-push finished, regctl returned status 200 for layer uploads. Now running skopeo inspect on the new prod image.

sara.oncall: skopeo inspect shows prod layer digests now: ```
{"size": 1248123, "digest": "sha256:111aaa..."}
{"size": 4096, "digest": "sha256:222bbb..."}
```
These match staging.

registry-bot: Manifest verification OK. staging digest sha256:aa11... equals prod digest sha256:aa11...

chris.sre: Great. Re-run deploybot promote check.

deploy-bot: Promotion preflight passed for redwood/api-service:2026-03-canary. No checksum mismatches detected. Ready to unhold.

amanda.release: Un-holding now and promoting. Note for release notes: "Canary promo briefly blocked due to manifest digest mismatch caused by non-deterministic compression in pushing pipeline; resolved by re-pushing deterministic blobs. Infra ticket created."

ben.infra: Ticket: INFRA-7892 posted with logs and suggested buildkite plugin changes.

chris.sre: Postmortem follow-up: make deterministic-build flag default in our image canonicalization step, and add a registry verification job in nightly to catch drift.

amanda.release: Thanks all. Marking this thread resolved. :white_check_mark: 

ben.infra: FYI leaving the pin in place for 15 minutes of traffic validation before we fully flip.

sara.oncall: Traffic looks normal, no errors in 10m window.

amanda.release: Ok to close then.

chris.sre: closing thread.
